title: fix(metadata-protocol): revertCommit reports a restored non-object item whose registry write-through faults
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbNTugWasvhTMrtCZiFGrZYK)_

Fixes #33851

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:撤销提交(revertCommit)现在对所有类型如实上报两类故障。第一类是恢复视图、权限、对象扩展等条目时,写入运行时注册表出错;这时该条目列入 failed[],写明「行已恢复到版本 N」。第二类是撤销删除条目后注册表修复(heal)中途停止;这时写明「行已从 sys_metadata 移除,注册表可能仍在提供被删的行」。两类都带出错原因和 code,success 为 false,和对象条目的处理一致。
- 为什么改:以前这些故障只记日志,撤销照样报 success:true,但进程实际还在使用旧内容,违反 revertCommit 自己的契约「success 即进程已生效」(ADR-0067 D3)。
- 风险与回滚:只有 revertCommit 读这两个新返回值。保存、发布、删除等其他调用方都忽略它们,同样的故障下仍答成功,日志也不变(有对照测试,另有消融证明对照测试能变红)。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`protocol-registry-hydration.ts` 中 `applyRegistryWriteThrough` 的两个 catch 和 `restoreArtifactRegistryView` 的外层 catch、剩余行循环;`protocol-package-commits.ts` 的 revertCommit 两个分支;`protocol.ts` 中两个转发方法的类型。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run src/protocol.revert-commit-honest-outcome.test.ts`,预期 31 个用例全绿(§3 共 12 个,§4 共 9 个)。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。#33563 那条变更说明里的一句旧话,在单独的纯文本 PR 中更正。

## What changes

`applyRegistryWriteThrough` has three branches. The `object` branch has answered the registry's refusal since #33805. The two non-object branches caught their faults and logged them at `warn`. The first is the overlay hydration, which every type except `object` and `object_extension` takes. The second is the `object_extension` registration. The registry heal that a removal runs (`restoreArtifactRegistryView`) logged its stop at `error` and returned nothing.

- `protocol-registry-hydration.ts`, write-through. The request has its own exported type, `RegistryWriteThroughRequest`, with one new optional field, `answerFaults`. When it is `true`, a non-object branch that throws still logs the same `warn` line, and then returns the fault in the `ObjectRegistryRefusal` shape (`{ error }`). When it is unset, the answer is `undefined`, as before.
- `protocol-registry-hydration.ts`, heal. `restoreArtifactRegistryView` now returns a `RegistryHealStop` (`{ error }`) in two cases. The first is when its outer catch stopped the walk; the `error` line it logs is unchanged. The second is when a row still stored under another package, which the heal registers again (with `answerFaults: true`), is refused or faults; every remaining row is still tried. Otherwise it returns `undefined`, and that includes the designed outcomes: a refused baseline read that retires the entry, and a degraded read that keeps it.
- `protocol-package-commits.ts`, `revertCommit`. The restore limb sets `answerFaults: true`. The soft-remove limb reads the heal's stop, but only where a row was actually removed; with no row removed, the heal is a self-heal and stays logged. Both feed the existing `notApplied` / `settle` path, so the item lands in `failed[]` with the row state, the reason and its `code`. The revert's own commit still records the row change. `rollbackToPackageCommit` carries the item through its existing per-item channel.
- `protocol.ts`, two private forwarders. The `restoreArtifactRegistryView` forwarder now returns `Promise` of `RegistryHealStop | undefined` (`ProtocolHost` derives its type from it). The `applyRegistryWriteThrough` forwarder's parameter is now `RegistryWriteThroughRequest`, in place of its inline copy. The `revertCommit` docblock sentence that said a non-object write-through fault "is not seen here" now says that every type, and a stopped heal, is reported. The `.d.ts` carries that docblock, so this change takes a `patch` changeset.
- Every other caller ignores the new answers. Save and publish (`protocol-save.ts`, `protocol-history-and-publish.ts`) do not set `answerFaults`. They would report any returned refusal as an object's (`object-registry-refused`), which ablation A4 shows. The delete door, a publish's undo and a peer's convergence `await` the heal and discard its answer.
- Changeset: `.changeset/33851-revert-non-object-write-through-fault.md` (`patch`). It says that it supersedes the sentence of the #33563 note claiming such a fault "is still not seen by the revert". The #33563 note itself is unchanged here: its one sentence is corrected in a separate text-only PR (DELIBERATE CORRECTION).

## Tests

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.revert-commit-honest-outcome.test.ts`, the revert harness, gains two top-level describes. They go there as AGENTS.md requires (ruling record 6583487846).

- §3 has 12 cases, 4 each for `view`, `permission` and `object_extension`: a clean restore control, which reaches the registry verb as a non-vacuity check; a write-through throw that goes to `failed[]` with `code`, "its row was restored to the body of version 1", the reason and `success: false`; a save control; and a publish control. The two controls hold under the same fault: `success: true`, no advisories, and the same `warn` line.
- §4 has 9 cases, 4 each for `view` and `permission`: a clean soft-remove control; a heal stop that goes to `failed[]` with `code`, "its row was removed from sys_metadata", "may still serve the removed row", `success: false` and the heal's `error` line kept; a delete control (`success: true`, `error` line kept); and a save-and-publish control (both `success: true`, no advisories). The ninth case is an `action` row still stored under another package that the registry refuses: it goes to `failed[]`. As a non-vacuity check, the stop is the remaining row's write-through `warn`, not the heal's outer-catch `error`.

Premise, measured on the code before each half. On the write-through half (source at `63e47feeca`), §3's 3 fault cases were red: each answered `success: true`. On the heal half (source at `2d23b49dd1`), §4's 3 fault cases were red, with 28 cases green.

<details><summary>Ablations (scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, each landed, run, then restored to blob == HEAD with git diff HEAD empty)</summary>

| Ablation | Red | Green |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1: the overlay branch does not answer | 2 (§3 view, permission fault) | 20 of 22 |
| A2: the extension branch does not answer | 1 (§3 object_extension fault) | 21 of 22 |
| A3: revertCommit does not set `answerFaults` | 3 (every §3 fault case) | 19 of 22 |
| A4: the overlay branch answers every caller | 4 (view and permission save and publish controls; the save answered an `object-registry-refused` advisory, "object 'ticket.grid' was published, but the runtime registry refused it") | 18 of 22 |
| A5: the extension branch answers every caller | 2 (object_extension save and publish controls) | 20 of 22 |
| B1: the heal's outer catch does not return its stop | 2 (§4 view, permission heal stop: "expected true to be false" on `success`) | 29 of 31 |
| B2: the remaining row's refusal is dropped | 1 (§4 remaining-row case) | 30 of 31 |
| B3: revertCommit does not read the heal's stop | 3 (every §4 fault case) | 28 of 31 |

My first A1 to A3 attempt was a no-op: the replacement was a substring of the anchor, `ablation-replace` refused it, and no test ran. They were re-run with distinct markers, and the table shows those runs. A1 to A5 were run before §4 existed (22 cases). B1 to B3 were run on all 31 cases.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Out of scope, left as it is: in the heal, the object owner branch's `unregisterObject` refusal ("object 'x' was deleted from sys_metadata but stays registered") is still a `warn` line that answers no stop. It is an object-only path, and the card's ruling covered the outer catch and the remaining rows.

## Verification

<details><summary>Readings, local, at head 999b09d9c3</summary>

- One locked run, at `999b09d9c3` with `origin/main` `68e726d631` merged in (lock VERDICT command-exit 0; queued 6m18s, after a first attempt's queue-timeout exit 99). It ran: the metadata-protocol dependency closure build; `typecheck` exit 0; `test` 342 files passed and 9 skipped, 22923 tests passed; the metadata-protocol build; and the objectql suite, 597 of 597 files and 13177 of 13177 tests.
- The other direct dependents (runtime, cli, service-automation, cloud-connection) were not run locally. CI runs them (Test Core). The only type that moved is on private forwarders; `RegistryHealStop` and `RegistryWriteThroughRequest` are not exported from the package entry.
- `pnpm lint`: exit 0.
- `dispatch-gates --ran`: 73 derived families, each with its exit code recorded. 70 exit 0. 3 are NOT MEASURED, because each needs the whole workspace built: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure` and `check:type-check-debt`, all exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET). CI runs them. The body gates (closing-keyword parity, Part-of, changeset no-major, ADR-0087 registration) exit 0.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only`: clean against `origin/main` `68e726d631`, against #33885's head `fa7fb66a7c`, and against S5's `claude/area-E1b-33832` head `9c4f75f36e`. No open PR for #33308 was found. No other open PR touches `protocol.ts`, `protocol-registry-hydration.ts`, `protocol-package-commits.ts` or the harness file.
- Dogfood: not run, because the title has no `!` and Clause-② has no (narrowing) arm.
</details>
